name: Franklin Covey Company
business_overview: Franklin Covey Co. provides training and consulting services in the areas of leadership, customer loyalty, execution, productivity, sales performance, and educational improvement for organizations and individuals worldwide. The company operates through four segments: North America, International Direct Offices, International Licensees, and Education Division. It offers a suite of individual-effectiveness and leadership-development training and products, such as The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People, The Speed of Trust, The Leader In Me, The Four Disciplines of Execution, Trust & Inspire, and Multipliers. The company also operates internet-based platforms, including All Access Pass and Leader in Me that offer training days and training course materials. The company was formerly known as Franklin Quest Co. and changed its name to Franklin Covey Co. in May 1997. Franklin Covey Co. was incorporated in 1983 and is based in Draper, Utah.

classification_meta.logic_summary: Provides training and consulting services to organizations and individuals.

narrative.text:
**Business & market dynamics:** Franklin Covey’s core Enterprise North America segment showed steady demand momentum, with invoiced amounts rising and a healthy buildup in deferred revenue. However, overall revenue growth was subdued, and the top line fell short of expectations, prompting a reduction in full-year guidance. The quarter marked a clear recovery in profitability after a prior-year loss, reflecting a stabilization in the business rather than broad-based acceleration. The picture is mixed: client engagement remains solid, but revenue conversion pressures persist, and the external demand environment appears cautious.

**Management strategy and execution:** Leadership has focused on operational discipline, as evidenced by the swing to net income and improved adjusted EBITDA following earlier restructuring actions. The company maintains a strong liquidity profile and fully available credit, while aggressively returning capital through share repurchases. The decision to trim full-year revenue guidance, even as profitability rebounds, signals a pragmatic, conservative outlook in the face of uneven revenue traction. The market is likely weighing this prudence against the credibility of the turnaround and the pace of organic growth.

# Franklin Covey (NYSE: FC) Reports Q3 Profit, Trims Guidance

By Patricia Miller

Jul 06, 2026

3 min read

Franklin Covey Co. (NYSE: FC) reported Q3 fiscal 2026 net income of $3.1 million and lowered its full-year revenue guidance to $260 million to $267 million.

Franklin Covey Co. (NYSE: FC) reported net income of $3.1 million, or $0.27 per diluted share, for the third quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with a net loss of $1.4 million, or $0.11 per share, in the same period a year earlier. The company also lowered its full-year revenue guidance in results announced July 1.

Consolidated revenue for the quarter, which ended May 31, 2026, rose 1% to $67.8 million from $67.1 million in the prior-year period.
